title: "Glioblastoma FFPE Tissues Dissociated Manually or using gentleMACS Dissociator, Multiplexed Samples, 4 Probe Barcodes (Next GEM)"
format: html

---

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(gprofiler2)
  library(scales)
})
```

We set the sample name and the seed to avoid random values

```{r}
sample.name<-"Brain_DV200"
species<-"Human"
```

```{r}
the.seed<-42
set.seed(the.seed)
```

```{r}
scmat<-Read10X("../data/raw_data/sample_raw_feature_bc_matrix")
```

```{r}
class(scmat)
head(scmat)
```

```{r}
nb_umi_by_barcode<- data.frame(
  nb_umi=Matrix::colSums(scmat),
  barcodes = colnames(scmat))


nb_umi_by_barcode<- nb_umi_by_barcode %>% arrange(desc(nb_umi)) %>% dplyr::mutate(num_barcode=seq.int(ncol(scmat)))

#knee plot
ggplot(nb_umi_by_barcode, aes(y = nb_umi, x = num_barcode)) +
  geom_point() + ggtitle(paste0("Kneeplot of ", sample.name, " sample")) +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_y_log10(name = "Number of UMI per droplet (log scale)") +
  scale_x_log10(name = "Droplet rank (log scale)") +
  expand_limits(x = 0, y = 0) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linetype = c(0, 0), shape = c(16, 16))))
```

The knee-plot look perfect, we have a unique knee at approx 3000umi, next step is to create a seurat object.

Note : this is the *raw* matrix (all barcodes, including empty droplets), so the gene/UMI filters below also act as the empty-droplet filter. Using `sample_filtered_feature_bc_matrix` (Cell Ranger cell calling) or `DropletUtils::emptyDrops` would be more rigorous.

```{r}
sobj <- CreateSeuratObject(
  counts = scmat,
  min.cells = 5,
  min.features = 200,
  project = sample.name)

```

```{r}
#class of our Seurat Object
class(sobj)
#barcodes names
head(sobj)
# number of barcodes
ncol(sobj)
# number of features
nrow(sobj)
# the object
sobj

```

Now that we have our Seurat object, `r ncol(sobj)` barcodes and `r nrow(sobj)` features (genes), lets free some memory

```{r}
rm(nb_umi_by_barcode, scmat)
gc()
```

```{r}
sobj@meta.data[1:10,]
sobj@assays$RNA@layers$counts[1:10,1:4]
```

Now lets filter our object, remove undersequenced cells, debris, duplicates or multiplets.

```{r}
summary(sobj$nFeature_RNA)

#histogram
hist(sobj$nFeature_RNA,
     breaks = 200,
     xlab = "number of genes",
     main = "number of genes per cell"
)
# violin plot
VlnPlot(sobj, features= c("nFeature_RNA"), alpha = 0.1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 800)

```

The violin plot is good to visualise the number of genes per cell, we can see a high density of barcodes in the bottom of the plot (median \~600 genes) which correspond to debris, dead cells or empty droplets, so we keep cells with more than 800 genes.

We do not apply an upper threshold on the number of genes : some real cells have a lot of genes (e.g. inhibitory neurons have a median of \~5000 genes and \~11k UMI in this dataset), a hard cut at 5000 genes would remove them. Doublets/multiplets are removed later with scDblFinder.

```{r}
summary(sobj$nCount_RNA)
#Violin plot (to see number of UMI (RNAs) per cell )
VlnPlot(sobj, features = c ("nCount_RNA"), alpha = 0.1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 1000)
#hard to visualise so lets log scale
VlnPlot(sobj, features = c ("nCount_RNA"),log=TRUE, alpha = 0.1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 1000)

```

```{r}
FeatureScatter(sobj, feature1="nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA", pt.size = 0.1)
```

Pearson correlation is 0.76 which is good, a minimum of 1000 UMI per cell removes the empty droplets and low quality cells.

```{r}
# lets define the thresholds based on Vlnplots
minGenes = 800
minUmi = 1000
```

```{r}
sobjFiltrd = subset(sobj, subset = nFeature_RNA > minGenes & nCount_RNA > minUmi)
```

ok now i've filtered the object on the thresholds defined, lets visualise before we clean the environment

```{r}
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), ncol = 2,pt.size = 0.01)

FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "nFeature_RNA",pt.size =0.1)
```

ok good, now lets process mitochondrial genes.

```{r}
mito_pattern <- "^MT-"
sobjFiltrd$percent_mt<- PercentageFeatureSet(sobjFiltrd, pattern = mito_pattern)
summary(sobjFiltrd$percent_mt)
```

```{r}
#Violin plot mito genes
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("percent_mt")) + geom_hline(yintercept = 10)
#histogram
ggplot(data.frame(percent_mt = sobjFiltrd$percent_mt), aes(x = percent_mt)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 100) + geom_vline(xintercept = 10) + ggtitle("percent_mt")

FeatureScatter(sobjFiltrd, feature1 = "nCount_RNA", feature2 = "percent_mt",pt.size =0.1)
```

The pearson correlation is negative (-0.14) : cells with a high % of mitochondrial genes have a low number of UMI (damaged/dying cells). Most cells are below 5%, but for FFPE tissue (Flex probe-based chemistry) a threshold of 10% is more usual and keeps \~370 more cells, so we use 10%.

```{r}
maxpct_mt = 10
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset =  percent_mt < maxpct_mt)
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), ncol = 2)
```

```{r}
ncol(sobjFiltrd) #Nbr of barcodes (cells)
nrow(sobjFiltrd) #Nbr of genes
```

now we ended up with `r ncol(sobjFiltrd)` cells and `r nrow(sobjFiltrd)` genes

we had `r ncol(sobj)` barcodes and the same number of genes

```{r}
rm(sobj)
gc()
```

Now we will remove doublets and multiplets using scDblFinder package, for this we need to convert the seurat object into other format using function : asSingleCellExperiment

```{r}
# Transforming Seurat object
sceobj<-as.SingleCellExperiment(sobjFiltrd)

#We remove doublets
set.seed(the.seed)
doublet_res<-scDblFinder(sceobj)

#We save the results in the Seurat object
sobjFiltrd$doublets.class <-doublet_res$scDblFinder.class

# % of doublets
table(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class)
round(100 * prop.table(table(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class)), 1)
```

We have `r round(100 * mean(sobjFiltrd$doublets.class == "doublet"), 1)`% of doublets which is not high, the dataset is clean.

now lets remove the doublets and visualise again

```{r}
sobjFiltrd <- subset(sobjFiltrd, subset = doublets.class == "singlet")
VlnPlot(sobjFiltrd, features = c("nFeature_RNA", "nCount_RNA"), ncol = 2)
```

```{r}
rm(doublet_res, sceobj)
gc()
```

Now after filtering Mitochondrial genes and doublets/multiplets + low quality cells, we have to normalise the data, since some cells have high number of umi than others, some cells are more active than others due to their biology, but we also have sequencing bias that we need to correct by normalizing or via integration if needed

```{r}
sobjFiltrd <- NormalizeData(sobjFiltrd, normalization.method = "LogNormalize")
```

We can also perform SCTransform, but this method does require some computational ressources since it uses GLMs to adjust residus.

now that we are done with QC step we go ahead and save

```{r}
# Save seurat object
save(sobjFiltrd, file = paste0('../data/processed_data/',sample.name,'_FILTERED.rda'))
```

```{r}
sessionInfo()
```
